page: Amazon Web Services r8a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or a GPU. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression tests scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is generally average, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput register in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks fall within the middle 50% range, while the Passmark memory score is in the top 25%.

Lacking local storage, the r8a.4xlarge relies entirely on network-attached storage, which represents a tradeoff for IOPS-heavy local database workloads. However, its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong single-core execution make it highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local disk caching. It is well-suited for in-memory databases, caching layers, data processing, and small-scale LLM inference tasks, where the 128 GB DDR5 RAM can be fully utilized.
